parts.title: The London Relocation Services
parts.transcript: S1: Anna Woods phones London Relocation Services (moving from near Belfast). Address 118 Fordyce (F-O-R-D-Y-C-E) Park, Ballysillan (1). Mobile 07840051963 (2). She's a qualified nurse and wants to get back into nursing (3; currently teaching assistant). Son still in primary school - needs a primary school (4). Husband's job in East London but they'd rather live somewhere quieter - lovely areas in the south (5). Husband wants to be near a station (6, not keen on buses). Son active - wants a park nearby (7). Always lived in a house, will stick with a house (8). Needs a three-bedroom property (9, for a guest room). A small office is also desirable (10, husband works from home).

parts.transcript: S2: manager on moving to a new office. Moving to be in a central location/city centre (clients won't come to the suburbs) (11=C; plenty of space already, current rent cheaper). Best feature = huge windows = natural light (12=B). Move as soon as the sales conference is over in January (13=A; finance wanted after tax year but they go earlier). Website already has restaurants/cafes = places to eat (14=B; transport & parking not yet up). Now: make a list of scratched/broken desks & chairs = give details of damaged furniture (15=A). Confidential folders go in grey plastic bags (16=B). Lifting: people forget to use the handles (D) and not to twist/lean to one side (C) (17/18=C,D; head up/back/feet apart already clear). Moving papers: use gloves (C) and drink plenty of water (E) (19/20=C,E; masks not necessary, windows can't open).

parts.transcript: S3: Mona & Ted discuss her presentation on design development. Mona focuses on the history of design from the 1800s (21=A; not the social-advancement/art-movement angles Ted suggested). She covered many areas because she was worried her teacher would think her lazy = afraid of tutor's response (22=A). Ted says the topic is too broad (23=C). Mona's view: computers have influenced traditional media more than the design industry (24=B); she'll use the traditional way. On purism: Ted disagrees it saves effort but thinks it's important to apply in architecture (25=A). Ted suggests she visit the design museum = visit a museum (26=C; she's read enough books). Presentation steps: Step1 write an introduction (27=D); Step2 research deeper into the topic (28=G); Step3 put a statement under each picture (29=E); Step5/final prepare text handouts (30=A). (Unused: questions B, an outline C, explain F.)

parts.transcript: S4: talk on the graphical symbol. Pictographs remain in common commercial (31) use today (signs, road signs, flat-pack instructions). Ancient graphic writing systems give researchers a wealth of knowledge (32) about past civilisations. Rosetta Stone (1799, Napoleon's expedition) deciphered by Champollion 1822; in the symbols, lines (33) are used to depict various meanings. Camera obscura -> photography (34) helps people understand history better. Animal welfare charities use photography to advertise (35) animals at high risk of endangerment. A recent campaign attached a camera to the foot (36) of a bird. Future: expect more objects (37) included as photography (drones) progresses. Media firms get income from advertising - companies devote big budgets to advertising in newspapers (38). Effective branding relies on attractive packaging (39). Graphic writing systems are of great importance in mathematics (40, e.g. graphs, periodic table).
